claims.text: The baseline eutectic high-entropy alloy is in an as-cast state with a coarse, less well-aligned eutectic microstructure.
Cold rolling followed by optimized annealing can refine the eutectic lamellae.
Cold rolling followed by optimized annealing can align the eutectic lamellae.
The treatment can improve interphase coherence.
Refined eutectic lamellae provide more numerous and effective barriers to dislocation motion.
More numerous and effective barriers to dislocation motion increase strength.
Improved lamellar alignment enhances deformation compatibility between the constituent phases.
Improved alignment and coherent interfaces facilitate uniform plastic deformation.
Improved alignment and coherent interfaces mitigate strain localization.
Facilitating uniform plastic deformation and mitigating strain localization improve ductility.
The thermomechanically treated alloy will have higher yield strength than the as-cast alloy.
The thermomechanically treated alloy will have greater elongation to failure than the as-cast alloy.
The intervention is expected to work when the two phases have sufficient mutual solubility to form coherent or semi-coherent interfaces.
The intervention requires optimization of strain rate, rolling reduction, annealing temperature, and annealing time.
The intervention may not work when severe chemical segregation is present.
The intervention may not work if processing makes one constituent phase too brittle.
Detrimental phase transformations could prevent the proposed simultaneous improvement in strength and ductility.
